The compatibility-versus-necessity distinction coherently blocks treating an explanation that merely fits an anecdote as established.
The methodological distinction has conceptual support, but the passage supplies little comparative evidence concerning the referenced anecdotes.
As an opening constructive, the move directly establishes the negative verification burden without assuming a contrary account of reality.
The distinction centrally supports the negative burden by showing that explanatory fit alone does not demonstrate the proposed soul explanation.
The core distinction is clear, but the demand for literal necessity is stronger than ordinary comparative explanation always requires.

The practical-label account weakens the soul inference but leaves the underlying metaphysical question of persistence unresolved.
The practical-label thesis is understandable, but the reply alternates between qualitative sameness and ordinary numerical identity.
